title: Plans for Willow Meadow Divide the Town
subject: English
source: Written for english/y3 lesson 81 (Teacher's news report and fact cards (lesson 80))
intro: Lesson 81. A made-up news report about a made-up town. Read it, sort the fact cards, then use them in your debate.

cards: 300 families could live on the meadow.
There are not enough houses in Brookfield.
The meadow flooded twice last winter.
blocks.task: sort them into Builders and Environmental group.
blocks.answer: Builders: 300 families; not enough houses; new jobs. Environmental group: river overflows; flooded twice; herons nest.

passage.title: Plans for Willow Meadow Divide the Town
paras: Plans to build 300 new homes on Willow Meadow have split the town of Brookfield in two.

On Monday, Greenfield Builders asked the council for permission to build on the meadow, which lies beside the River Brook. 'Families need homes,' said a spokesperson for the builders. 'There are not enough houses in Brookfield, and 300 families could live here. The work will also bring new jobs.'

Not everyone agrees. The Brookfield Environmental Group says the land is not safe to build on. 'The meadow floods,' explained its leader. 'The river overflows in winter, and it flooded twice last winter. Herons nest there every spring, and many birds and insects live in the long grass. Once it is built on, it is gone forever.'
The council will decide next month. Until then, both sides are asking people to share their views.

questions.q: Who wants to build on Willow Meadow?
How many homes do they want to build?
Give one reason the Environmental Group gives against building.
questions.a: The land floods (twice last winter), or herons and other wildlife live there.

questions.q: Add a reason: We should build homes ___.
questions.a: For example: because families need somewhere to live

questions.q: Add evidence to: The land is wet.
questions.a: For example: It flooded twice last winter.
For example: It will bring new jobs.

questions.q: Core: in your group, write 2 points with Because and Evidence
questions.a: Two Point-Because-Evidence points for your side

questions.q: Extend: write one counter-argument and your answer
questions.a: For example: They say families need homes; we say build them on safer land.

questions.q: Stretch: write an opening line for your speech
questions.a: For example: Ladies and gentlemen, the meadow must be saved!

options: Families need homes because many are waiting.
questions.a: B) Families need homes because many are waiting.. It has a reason (because many are waiting). The others have no reason.
